title: Gehazi runs after Naaman for gifts — 2 Kings 5
paragraphs: Gehazi runs after Naaman for gifts — 2 Kings 5
And lost his soul in the dust behind Naaman’s chariot.

Gehazi had seen a miracle with his own eyes. Naaman the leper walked away clean. Grace had just filled the room. Mercy had just spoken. But Gehazi could not stand to watch someone leave without squeezing profit out of the moment.

Not for God.
Not for truth.
For gifts.

He lied to Naaman.
He lied to Elisha.
But the deadliest lie was the one in his own heart: I can touch holy things and still hide greed.
And that is where many fall.

You can stand near miracles and still be mastered by money.
You can serve in ministry and still be starving in secret.
You can look close to the prophet and be far from God.

But here’s what we miss: Gehazi’s story is not just about greed. It is about a heart that wanted the benefits of God without the fear of God. He wanted the blessing, but not the holiness. The reward, but not the surrender.

Some people are not ruined by persecution.
They are ruined by opportunity.
2 Kings 5 shows us a man who traded grace for garments, silver, and status — and what he gained for a moment cost him far more than he imagined.
But thanks be to Jesus, our story does not have to end like Gehazi’s.

Where greed corrupts, Christ cleanses.
Where sin hides, Christ exposes and heals.
Where shame settles in, Christ still calls sinners to repent and come home.

Bring the secret thing into the light.
Drop the lie.
Stop running after what God never told you to chase.

There is mercy even for hearts that have wandered.
There is cleansing deeper than leprosy.
There is a Savior greater than your sin.
